observations: Large industrial diesel engine block, grayish-green paint, heavily weathered with rust and dirt.
Engine sits on a wooden pallet on muddy ground in what looks like a scrapyard or workshop yard.
A round emblem/logo is visible on the side of the engine block, but the text on it is not legible at this resolution.
No visible data plate, serial tag, or model sticker that can be read.
Wiring harness and hoses are disconnected and dangling, consistent with a removed/stored engine.
Large flywheel housing visible at the front, heavily rusted on the outer ring.
Green metal structures and a tank in the background suggest an industrial/marine salvage yard setting.
No visible turbocharger, alternator, or starter motor attached - engine may be partially stripped.
No way to see fluid levels, oil condition, or hear/see the engine running.

claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows a round emblem on the engine block but no readable brand/model text or data plate; claim cannot be confirmed from the image alone.

risks.risk: True brand/model unconfirmed - price for a 'Detroit 6-71' varies hugely from a generic unbranded marine diesel.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the engine's data plate/serial tag or any legible cast lettering on the block.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a generic unidentified marine diesel engine, not as a branded Detroit 671

risks.risk: Engine may be incomplete (missing turbocharger, alternator, starter, injectors visible in photo).
risks.proof: Full walk-around photos from both sides and rear showing all accessory mounting points.

risks.risk: Running condition unverified - heavy external rust and outdoor storage suggest possible internal corrosion or seizure.
risks.proof: Video clip of the engine being started and running, or at least turning over.

risks.risk: Exposure to weather (mud, rain) raises risk of water ingress into cylinders or electrical damage.
risks.proof: Photo of air intake and exhaust openings, and confirmation of how long it has been stored outdoors.

risks.risk: Pallet/skid suggests engine may have been dropped or handled roughly, risking hidden mechanical damage.
risks.proof: Photos of mounting feet, oil pan, and crankshaft pulley for impact damage.
risks.if_unproven: priced as condition unknown, treated as damaged until shown otherwise

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the engine's serial/data plate or any cast model markings.
Video of the engine cranking or running.
Additional photos from the opposite side and rear showing completeness of accessories (turbo, alternator, starter, injection pump).
Photo showing oil dipstick/oil condition and coolant reservoir if present.
response.reason: The seller's claimed brand and model cannot be read from the single photo, and this identity is the main driver of price for an industrial marine engine; a legible data plate or model photo is needed before even a worst-case price can be set.
